# Renewable Energy Cost Revolution: LCOE, Capacity & Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)

## Overview
This collection of four datasets tracks the economic transformation of the global energy sector from 2010 to 2024. It covers the declining levelized cost of energy for solar PV, onshore wind, and battery storage; the cost range of new fossil fuel generation; cumulative renewable installed capacity; and annual global fossil fuel subsidies.

## Data Source

### lcoe_trends
Annual LCOE values for three technologies: `solar_pv`, `onshore_wind`, and `battery_storage`. All values in 2023 real USD per MWh. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV ranges from 359 to 33; onshore wind from 95 to 35; battery storage from 1,100 to 102.

### fossil_fuel_lcoe_range
Biennial LCOE ranges for new-build gas CCGT (`gas_ccgt_low`, `gas_ccgt_high`) and coal (`coal_low`, `coal_high`). 8 rows at even-year intervals. Values in 2023 real USD/MWh. These define the reference band against which renewable crossover points are identified.

### installed_capacity
Cumulative global installed capacity in GW for `solar_pv_gw` and `onshore_wind_gw`. 15 rows (2010–2024). Solar PV grows from 40 to 1,950 GW; onshore wind from 178 to 960 GW.

### fossil_fuel_subsidies
Annual global fossil fuel subsidies in nominal billion USD, split into `consumption_subsidies_bn` and `production_subsidies_bn`, with a `total_subsidies_bn` sum. 15 rows (2010–2024). Total ranges from ~290 to ~700 billion.

## Data Notes
- LCOE figures are illustrative estimates aligned with IRENA and BloombergNEF reporting trends but rounded for clarity.
- Battery storage LCOE reflects 4-hour lithium-ion systems.
- 2022 spike in fossil LCOE and subsidies reflects the global energy price crisis.
- Fossil fuel subsidy estimates cover direct government subsidies only; implicit subsidies (e.g., unpriced externalities) are excluded.
- 2024 values are preliminary estimates.

import json
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.ticker as ticker
from matplotlib.patches import Patch
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
from scipy.interpolate import interp1d

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

lcoe_data = data['lcoe_trends']['data']
years = [d['year'] for d in lcoe_data]
solar_lcoe = [d['solar_pv'] for d in lcoe_data]
wind_lcoe = [d['onshore_wind'] for d in lcoe_data]
battery_lcoe = [d['battery_storage'] for d in lcoe_data]

fossil_data = data['fossil_fuel_lcoe_range']['data']
fossil_years = [d['year'] for d in fossil_data]
fossil_min = [min(d['gas_ccgt_low'], d['coal_low']) for d in fossil_data]
fossil_max = [max(d['gas_ccgt_high'], d['coal_high']) for d in fossil_data]

# Interpolate fossil data to match all years
f_min_interp = interp1d(fossil_years, fossil_min, kind='linear', fill_value="extrapolate")
f_max_interp = interp1d(fossil_years, fossil_max, kind='linear', fill_value="extrapolate")
fossil_min_all = f_min_interp(years)
fossil_max_all = f_max_interp(years)

cap_data = data['installed_capacity']['data']
solar_cap = [d['solar_pv_gw'] for d in cap_data]
wind_cap = [d['onshore_wind_gw'] for d in cap_data]

sub_data = data['fossil_fuel_subsidies']['data']
sub_total = [d['total_subsidies_bn'] for d in sub_data]
sub_cons = [d['consumption_subsidies_bn'] for d in sub_data]
sub_prod = [d['production_subsidies_bn'] for d in sub_data]

# Styling
plt.style.use('default')
fig, (ax1, ax2, ax3) = plt.subplots(3, 1, figsize=(12, 16), sharex=True, gridspec_kw={'height_ratios': [2, 1.2, 1.2]})
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff')

# Colors
c_solar = '#FF9F1C'
c_wind = '#2EC4B6'
c_battery = '#9B5DE5'
c_fossil = '#5A5A5A'
c_subsidy_c = '#E76F51'
c_subsidy_p = '#F4A261'
text_color = '#333333'

# --- PANEL 1: LCOE ---
ax1.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
ax1.grid(True, axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, color='#cccccc')
ax1.grid(True, axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.2, color='#cccccc')

# Fossil band
ax1.fill_between(years, fossil_min_all, fossil_max_all, color=c_fossil, alpha=0.15, label='_nolegend_')
ax1.plot(years, fossil_min_all, color=c_fossil, alpha=0.5, linestyle=':', linewidth=1)
ax1.plot(years, fossil_max_all, color=c_fossil, alpha=0.5, linestyle=':', linewidth=1)

# LCOE Lines
ax1.plot(years, battery_lcoe, color=c_battery, linewidth=3.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Battery Storage (4-hr)')
ax1.plot(years, solar_lcoe, color=c_solar, linewidth=3.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Solar PV')
ax1.plot(years, wind_lcoe, color=c_wind, linewidth=3.5, marker='o', markersize=5, label='Onshore Wind')

ax1.set_yscale('log')
ax1.set_yticks([30, 50, 100, 300, 1000])
ax1.get_yaxis().set_major_formatter(ticker.ScalarFormatter())
ax1.set_ylabel('Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE)\nUSD/MWh (2023 real dollars)', fontsize=12, color=text_color, fontweight='bold')
ax1.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=11, colors=text_color)
ax1.set_ylim(25, 1300)

# Annotations Panel 1
# Battery collapse
ax1.annotate('Dramatic 91% cost collapse\nfrom $1,100 to $102/MWh', 
             xy=(2010, 1100), xytext=(2011.5, 1100),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor=c_battery, shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6, edgecolor='none'),
             fontsize=11, color=c_battery, fontweight='bold', va='center')

# Crossover points
# Solar crosses fossil min in 2020 (42 vs 45)
ax1.annotate('Solar crosses below\nfossil cost range', 
             xy=(2020, 42), xytext=(2017.5, 26),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor=c_solar, shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6, edgecolor='none'),
             fontsize=11, color='#d35400', fontweight='bold', ha='center')

# Wind crosses fossil min in ~2020 (41 vs 45)
ax1.annotate('Wind consistently\nbelow fossil range', 
             xy=(2019, 44), xytext=(2021.5, 26),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor=c_wind, shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6, edgecolor='none'),
             fontsize=11, color='#00796B', fontweight='bold', ha='center')

ax1.text(2023.5, 80, 'Fossil Fuel\nCost Range', color=c_fossil, fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', ha='center', va='center')

ax1.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=False, fontsize=12)
ax1.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax1.spines['left'].set_color('#cccccc')
ax1.spines['bottom'].set_color('#cccccc')


# --- PANEL 2: Installed Capacity ---
ax2.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
ax2.grid(True, axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, color='#cccccc')
ax2.grid(True, axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.2, color='#cccccc')

ax2.fill_between(years, 0, solar_cap, color=c_solar, alpha=0.7, label='Solar PV')
ax2.fill_between(years, solar_cap, np.array(solar_cap) + np.array(wind_cap), color=c_wind, alpha=0.7, label='Onshore Wind')

ax2.set_ylabel('Cumulative Installed\nCapacity (GW)', fontsize=12, color=text_color, fontweight='bold')
ax2.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=11, colors=text_color)
ax2.set_ylim(0, 3200)

# Annotation Panel 2
ax2.annotate('Steep acceleration in\nSolar PV post-2018', 
             xy=(2021, 800), xytext=(2015, 1200),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor=c_solar, shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6, edgecolor='none'),
             fontsize=11, color='#b94a00', fontweight='bold')

ax2.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=False, fontsize=12)
ax2.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax2.spines['left'].set_color('#cccccc')
ax2.spines['bottom'].set_color('#cccccc')


# --- PANEL 3: Fossil Fuel Subsidies ---
ax3.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
ax3.grid(True, axis='y', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5, color='#cccccc')
ax3.grid(True, axis='x', linestyle='--', alpha=0.2, color='#cccccc')

bar_width = 0.6
ax3.bar(years, sub_cons, width=bar_width, color=c_subsidy_c, alpha=0.85, label='Consumption Subsidies')
ax3.bar(years, sub_prod, width=bar_width, bottom=sub_cons, color=c_subsidy_p, alpha=0.85, label='Production Subsidies')

ax3.set_ylabel('Global Fossil Fuel\nSubsidies (Billion USD)', fontsize=12, color=text_color, fontweight='bold')
ax3.tick_params(axis='x', labelsize=12, colors=text_color)
ax3.tick_params(axis='y', labelsize=11, colors=text_color)
ax3.set_ylim(0, 800)
ax3.set_xticks(years)
ax3.set_xticklabels([str(y) for y in years], rotation=45)

# Annotation Panel 3
ax3.annotate('Subsidies persist & spike during crises,\ndespite falling renewable costs', 
             xy=(2022, 700), xytext=(2015.5, 650),
             arrowprops=dict(facecolor=c_subsidy_c, shrink=0.05, width=1, headwidth=6, edgecolor='none'),
             fontsize=11, color='#902910', fontweight='bold')

ax3.legend(loc='upper right', frameon=False, fontsize=12)
ax3.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax3.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax3.spines['left'].set_color('#cccccc')
ax3.spines['bottom'].set_color('#cccccc')


# Title and Super Title
fig.suptitle('The Clean Energy Cost Revolution vs. Persistent Fossil Fuel Subsidies (2010–2024)', 
             fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', color='#111111', y=0.96)
fig.text(0.5, 0.925, 
         'While solar, wind, and battery costs have plummeted below fossil fuels, spurring exponential capacity growth,\nglobal subsidies for fossil fuels remain volatile and remarkably high.', 
         ha='center', fontsize=13, color='#444444', style='italic')

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.91])
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
print("Successfully generated chart.")
EOF
